EXPLANATION: The spectrum is characteristic of a saturated, branched/cyclic hydrocarbon: very strong CH stretch at 2927 cm⁻¹ and strong CH₂ scissoring near 1436 cm⁻¹ (GFQ-003), moderate CH₃ deformation around 1360 cm⁻¹, and prominent C–C skeletal stretches near 1067–1096 cm⁻¹ (consistent with single-bond region; GFQ-010). The cluster of ring-type modes at 797/834/864 cm⁻¹ aligns well with cyclohexane breathing/deformation features, and the absence of a strong diagnostic band near 2200–2300 cm⁻¹ rules out isocyanate (candidate 5) or diazo (candidate 9). No clear O–H stretch near 3200–3600 cm⁻¹ is observed, making alcohol-containing candidates less likely. Among the hydrocarbons, a substituted cyclohexane (candidate 2) best matches this Raman pattern.
